breaking.headline: Nvidia forms national-security committee hours before earnings
breaking.fact: Nvidia created a board-level National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee on Tuesday, chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson, as fallout continues from Jensen Huang’s resignation over an affair with a woman U.S. officials suspect was recruited by Chinese intelligence; the board has hired Wachtell Lipton to investigate whether Huang shared confidential information. Tonight’s Q3 report — the first under interim CEO Colette Kress, consensus near $2.47 a share on about $109 billion in revenue — is the week’s main event; shares are up about 1% pre-market to near $158 after falling 4.12% Monday.

breaking.headline: Anthropic book closes today, about 7x oversubscribed; pricing tomorrow
breaking.fact: Orders for Anthropic’s IPO are running close to seven times the 825 million shares on offer, Bloomberg reported, and Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley expect to close the order book Tuesday. Pricing is set for Wednesday, Nov. 18, with trading to begin Thursday on Nasdaq as ANT at $70 to $78 a share; bankers are weighing a price above the range, and seven strategic partners including Google, Nvidia and Microsoft have agreed to buy $26 billion of stock in a private placement.

breaking.headline: Ukraine collapses Kerch Bridge span; Russia hits Kyiv bridges
breaking.fact: Ukrainian missiles and drones collapsed a road span of the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea overnight, and Russia confirmed the damage; Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv’s North and South bridges over the Dnipro late Monday, disrupting heating, water and power. U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said progress is being made toward ending the war, but important challenges remain.

breaking.headline: U.S. intel: Iran drew up dirty-bomb plot aimed at Washington
breaking.fact: New U.S. intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials in Washington with a radioactive “dirty bomb” or a chemical weapon, U.S. officials told CNN on Monday night. President Trump said he takes the report “very seriously”; the White House said there is no credible threat to the homeland right now.

weekInBrief.headline: Pentagon fails its financial audit for a ninth straight year
weekInBrief.body: Independent auditors again issued a disclaimer of opinion on the Pentagon’s fiscal 2026 books, saying the department could not provide enough reliable evidence to verify accounts covering more than $4.8 trillion in assets — the ninth consecutive year the world’s largest military has failed its audit.

weekInBrief.headline: Commerce moves to close the AI-chip remote-access loophole
weekInBrief.body: The Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim final rule on Nov. 16 further restricting companies in controlled countries from remotely using advanced U.S. AI chips and servers via third-country data centers — closing a workaround Nvidia had warned could expose it and its customers to U.S. penalties, as the White House tightens chip controls ahead of Trump’s talks with Xi Jinping.

weekInBrief.headline: Japan scrambles jets after suspected Russian airspace violation
weekInBrief.body: Japan said it launched fighter jets and “strongly” protested after two suspected Russian aircraft violated Japanese airspace early Tuesday morning — the latest in a run of Russian airspace incidents around U.S. allies in Asia and Europe.

weekInBrief.headline: Xi and Carney agree tariff cuts as Canada-China ties thaw
weekInBrief.body: Xi Jinping and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney agreed on additional tariff cuts between their nations and pledged deeper ties, a notable thaw in a relationship frozen for years, as President Trump travels to Asia for Thursday’s first-ever three-way summit with Xi and Vladimir Putin.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: UK Maritime Trade Operations reported two attacks on commercial tankers in the strait on Monday — one struck by an unknown projectile while leaving the strait, starting an engine-room fire, with the crew all accounted for; maritime security firm Vanguard Tech identified the ship as the Panama-flagged On Phoenix, hit about seven nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman. Iran’s Revolutionary Guards claimed two tankers caught fire after striking naval mines and that a supertanker carrying more than two million barrels of crude sank — none of the claims has been independently verified, and Reuters could not verify the mine claims. Etihad cancelled all passenger and cargo flights between Abu Dhabi and Riyadh and Dammam through Thursday, Nov. 19, and Europe’s aviation safety agency extended its Gulf conflict-zone advisory through Jan. 31, 2027. On oil, the blockade still holds — Kpler’s latest figures put oil and product flows through the strait at about 8.3 million barrels a day in the week to Nov. 11, roughly 48% of pre-war volumes, with Iranian-origin cargoes still excluded throughout, and Kpler data cited in reporting still puts Iranian shipments at zero since Aug. 25.

space.headline: Starship booster abort under investigation as NASA hails the historic catch
space.body: SpaceX is still investigating why Booster 22’s catch aborted minutes after liftoff — the company first pointed to a guidance problem, then said its systems detected a fuel-system alarm and triggered the abort, and the booster was destroyed offshore. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman called Ship 42’s first-ever orbital catch “almost magic,” and SpaceX plans to begin launching Starships from Kennedy Space Center in Florida within the next few months.

space.headline: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth on Wednesday
space.body: NASA’s Voyager 1 becomes the first human-made object to sit one full light-day from Earth — 16.094 billion miles — at 5:16 a.m. ET Wednesday, 49 years, two months and 11 days after launch. NASA is marking the night with its “Shine Bright for Voyager’s Light-Day” event, inviting people to flash V-G-R in Morse code skyward after sunset Tuesday.

space.headline: Neanderthal DNA linked to lower schizophrenia risk
space.body: A specific segment of Neanderthal DNA helps shape the modern human brain and is associated with a nearly 10% lower risk of schizophrenia in people carrying two copies, a study in PNAS found, based on UK Biobank data. The variant, near a gene involved in early brain development, was not linked to depression, bipolar disorder, ADHD or intelligence.

space.headline: Humpback whale ‘snot’ yields whole genomes without touching the whales
space.body: Researchers sequenced whole humpback whale genomes from samples of the whales’ blow — the mist they exhale at the surface — without darts, biopsies or close boat approaches. Fifty-eight blow samples from 26 whales yielded a population-level genome dataset for North Pacific humpbacks, published Nov. 17 in Molecular Ecology Resources.

apod.title: Milky Way versus Aurora
apod.credit: Guillaume Scheib — NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day, November 17, 2026
apod.explanation: Are these two giant arches battling for control of the sky? No, but it sure looks like it. The arch on the left is the central band of our Milky Way Galaxy, an ancient system of stars, gas and dust that predates Earth. The arch on the right is an auroral ribbon only hours old, made of energized atoms and molecules in Earth’s upper atmosphere. Far behind the auroral arch is the Big Dipper, and farther still the Andromeda galaxy — the bright spot near the top of the frame, just left of center. The image was taken about a month ago from Kvaløya in northern Norway.
